payload.answer: CONTROLLER-RESOLVED, not a resource limit and not surfaced to the human. The 'budget-exhausted / wave interrupted' label is a misattribution by slice-wave.workflow.js's catch-all at :520-521, which wraps ANY thrown JS error - including a plain TypeError - as a budget escalation. The real fault: TASK_RESULT does not list 'commits' in its required array, so a task may legitimately return DONE with no commit, but :433 reads r.commits.head unguarded. The sibling reads at :484 (fix) and :514 (debug-fix) DO guard the identical access. Journal wf_ab3d8f72-2b0 shows the cause exactly: results 3-6 are tasks t1-t4 with real commit pairs chaining fe288d8 -> eb85195 -> dec295a -> acec853, and result 7 is t5 returning status DONE, commits null, one touched file. t5 is the plan's verification-and-manifest-audit task, which by design changes nothing when the manifest is already correct - so a commit-less DONE is the CORRECT return, and the pipeline crashed on well-formed input. No work was lost: the s2 worktree is clean at acec853 with all six commits present, and the controller independently re-audited the manifest (run_state.py shim 928 of 929 lines, run_metrics.py 2074 of 2075, dag.py 786 of 787 left untouched as not this slice's file) and confirms all three entries correct. Resolution: guard the :433 read in this run's persisted workflow script copy and resume with resumeFromRunId, so plan, critique and t1-t5 replay from the journal cache and the pipeline continues into the review, gate and verify stages it never reached. A plain resume without the guard would re-crash deterministically, because t5's prompt is unchanged and would replay the same commit-less result into the same unguarded read.

This is a real defect in slice-wave.workflow.js 2.1.0, not a config problem: a commit-less DONE is a schema-valid and semantically correct return for a verification task, and the pipeline crashed on well-formed input.
